requirement_text.REQ-001a: GitHub issue #2 ("Translate to UZ" / "Add localization") requires Uzbek localization of the AI Qadam landing site. This requirement is the first of two: it proves the i18n MECHANISM end-to-end (dependency, routing, middleware/proxy, a working switcher) using only src/app/layout.tsx's strings as the seed catalog. Acceptance criteria: (1) Visiting /uz renders <html lang="uz">, visiting /ru (or /) renders <html lang="ru">; (2) clicking the Nav.tsx locale switcher's UZ control while on any /ru/* page navigates to the equivalent /uz/* page (same section anchors preserved), and clicking RU while on /uz/* navigates back to /ru/*; (3) next-intl is a dependency, npm run build completes with no type/routing errors; (4) messages/ru.json and messages/uz.json have matching key sets, every uz value non-empty (placeholder duplicate of ru acceptable); (5) the Nav.tsx switcher offers exactly two options RU and UZ (no EN), using only existing .lang/.lang a/.lang .on classes, no new hex/spacing values.

task.description: Run the scope test first per WF-02 Step 3: this requirement clearly has real user-visible surface (a rendered page with a working language switcher), so continue to the full procedure — do not skip to RELEASE-VALIDATOR. Write docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-001a.md: for each of REQ-001a's 5 acceptance criteria (listed in this handoff's context.requirement_text), write a concrete verification case naming the exact route (/, /ru, /uz, and specific in-page section anchors if relevant), exact viewport(s) (a mobile width and a desktop width per frontend_developer_guide.md's self-review checklist), exact theme(s) if applicable (note: REVIEWER already confirmed src/app/globals.css has no light/dark split for this component, so state explicitly that theme-checking doesn't apply here rather than inventing a case for it), and the exact expected behavior/output a TEST-RUNNER can check mechanically without judgment calls (e.g. 'curl -s http://localhost:3000/uz | grep -o "<html lang=\"[a-z]*\"" should output <html lang="uz">', not 'check the language looks right').
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-001a's 5 acceptance criteria has at least one verification case that would fail if violated
Each case names the exact route/URL, viewport (mobile/desktop pixel width or breakpoint), and expected result/output
No 'check it looks right' or other judgment-requiring language anywhere in the spec
No TODO left in the spec

result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-001a.md covering all 5 acceptance criteria with mechanical verification cases derived from the actual running implementation (verified via npm run build, a local dev-server curl session, and static-source grep checks), not guessed API behavior. AC1: exact curl+grep commands for /uz, /ru, and / (confirmed / does a 307 redirect to /ru, both resolving to the correct attribute). AC2: click-through cases at 600px and 1024px viewports (real breakpoints below/above globals.css's max-width:980px and max-width:620px media queries, per grep -n @media), plus a section-anchor case documenting the switcher's actual current behavior (links target bare /ru and /uz with no hash, since LocaleSwitcher.tsx builds hrefs from usePathname() only). Confirmed via curl that .lang is not hidden by any media query (only .nav-links collapses at 980px), so the switcher must remain clickable at the mobile width. AC3: npm run build verified to pass cleanly (exit 0, route table includes ƒ /[locale] and ƒ Proxy (Middleware)); next-intl confirmed present under dependencies (^4.13.7) via npm pkg get. AC4: a node one-liner recursively diffs message-key sets and flags empty uz values; verified ru.json and uz.json currently match with no empty values. AC5: curl+grep the exact expected

markup on both locales (2 links, RU/UZ, no EN); grep-verified LocaleSwitcher.tsx uses only className literals "lang" and "on"; grep-verified globals.css has exactly 3 .lang-prefixed selectors; and inspected the actual REQ-001a implementation commit (59596fc) diff to globals.css, which contains exactly one line changed (selector .lang span renamed to .lang a, no new hex/spacing) -- spec instructs TEST-RUNNER to re-locate the correct commit SHA if it differs on the branch under test.
